ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an organic chemistry transition-state structure, with multiple curved arrows present; the problem requires ignoring these arrows. In the actual skeleton, there is a benzene ring on the left, and the benzene ring is connected to a nitrogen atom bearing H. This nitrogen atom is connected to the central enamine fragment. The central part has a C=C double bond; one alkene carbon is connected to the nitrogen-containing substituent, and the other alkene carbon is simultaneously connected to the ethoxycarbonyl EtO-C(=O)- on the left and the CO2Et substituent on the right. The abbreviation EtO on the left represents -OCH2CH3, and CO2Et on the right represents -C(=O)OCH2CH3. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, only atoms and bonds need to be encoded. The ethoxycarbonyl on the left is written as CCOC(=O)-. The central malonate-type alkene carbon is connected to the left carbonyl carbon and the right carbonyl carbon, and forms a double bond with the carbon bearing the anilino substituent, so the central fragment can be written as C(=CNc1ccccc1). The CO2Et on the right is expanded as C(=O)OCC. Merging according to the path from the left ethyl ester carbonyl through the central alkene and then to the right ethyl ester gives the SMILES: CCOC(=O)C(=CNc1ccccc1)C(=O)OCC.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First visually identify only the atoms and bonds in the transition-state drawing, ignoring the arrows. Expand the abbreviated groups: the left EtO carbonyl becomes CCOC(=O)- and the right CO2Et becomes -C(=O)OCC. Encode the central malonate alkene carbon as attached to both ester carbonyl carbons and double-bonded to the carbon bearing the anilino substituent. Encode the anilino group as =CNc1ccccc1. Traversing from the left ethoxy ester through the central alkene and then to the right ester gives the SMILES CCOC(=O)C(=CNc1ccccc1)C(=O)OCC.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个有机化学过渡态结构，存在多条弯曲箭头；题目要求忽略这些箭头。实际骨架中，左侧有一个苯环，苯环连接到一个带 H 的氮原子。该氮原子连接到中央烯胺片段。中央部分有一个 C=C 双键；其中一个烯烃碳连接到含氮取代基，另一个烯烃碳同时连接左侧的乙氧羰基 EtO-C(=O)- 和右侧的 CO2Et 取代基。左侧缩写 EtO 表示 -OCH2CH3，右侧 CO2Et 表示 -C(=O)OCH2CH3。
推理：忽略箭头后，只需编码原子和键。左侧乙氧羰基写作 CCOC(=O)-。中央丙二酸酯型烯烃碳连接左侧羰基碳和右侧羰基碳，并与带 anilino 取代基的碳形成双键，因此中央片段可写为 C(=CNc1ccccc1)。右侧 CO2Et 展开为 C(=O)OCC。按从左乙酯羰基经过中央烯烃再到右乙酯的路径合并，得到 SMILES：CCOC(=O)C(=CNc1ccccc1)C(=O)OCC。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the straightforward single-route solution: transcribe the depicted static molecular graph while deliberately discarding the curved electron-flow arrows. For this problem there is not a genuinely different independent reasoning route beyond graph-to-SMILES transcription.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as a chemical structure: a benzene ring bonded to an N-H, the N bonded to a vinylic carbon in a C=N/C=C fragment, and a malonate-like carbon bearing two ethoxycarbonyl substituents, one drawn as EtO-C(=O)- and the other labeled CO2Et. Ignore all curved arrows and lone-pair motion annotations.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that the requested output is the SMILES expression of the shown transition-state structure and that the arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard SMILES conventions: EtO is CCO, an ethyl ester is CCOC(=O)- or -C(=O)OCC depending on traversal, benzene attached through nitrogen is Nc1ccccc1, and the drawn double bond is encoded with '='. Hydrogens on neutral amine nitrogen can be implicit in this context.
